title.narrative: Integrated Resiliency Building -WASH,Food Security Initiatives in South Kivu-DRC

description.narrative: The project aims to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable populations, particularly women and girls, in the districts of Mwenga, Walungu and Kabare in South Kivu, through an integrated ONE HEALTH approach. The project will improve access to water for irrigation, consumption and hygiene, boost food production and security, support sustainable livelihoods and promote good practices in health, the environment and nutrition. The project will also contribute to the prevention of zoonotic diseases and the strengthening of protection mechanisms, particularly for women who are victims of gender -based violence. To implement this project, Oxfam will work in financial partnership with two national organisations, APDIK (Farmers' Association for Integrated Development in South Kivu) and JSD (Youth for Solidarity and Development in the Great Lakes Region), as well as government technical services specializing in the project's key sectors. These two organizations will work closely with Oxfam to contribute to the sustainable strengthening of the resilience of the most vulnerable populations (host and displaced populations, particularly women and girls) exposed to health, food and protection risks in the territories of Mwenga, Walungu and Kabare, South Kivu province,in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as part of an integrated ‘ONE HEALTH' approach. This will be achieved through: - Improving access to water for field irrigation, consumption and personal hygiene, and enhancing economic security for vulnerable populations in the project's target areas. - Strengthening resilience and food security by boosting food production and promoting good practices for a balanced diet in the project's target areas - Preventing and mitigating the impact of epidemics, diseases and zoonoses (Mpox) in the project's target areas through ‘One Health' best practices. - Supporting referral systems to improve access to healthcare services for women who are victims of Gender Based Violence (GBV
